title: GPU memory bisect + tracebacks (personal scratchpad)
content:
Context:
- Personal debugging scratchpad for recurring GPU OOMs and occasional driver/runtime mismatches seen on my dev workstation and in a CI container image.
- Goal: capture commands tried, raw errors, hypotheses, and a short bisect plan so I can hand off to SRE if needed.

Timeline / quick notes:
- 2024-08-07: First saw intermittent OOM on a small batch job (batch_size=2) after a long training loop.
- 2024-09-12: Reproduced inside docker image runtime: nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime with pytorch wheel built against CUDA 11.8 — suspect ABI mismatch.
- 2025-01-10: Kernel update on laptop (linux 6.4) then more frequent crashes with dmesg showing Xid 31 and NVRM messages.

Commands (breadcrumbs):
- nvidia-smi -q -x  # dump state (driver, GPU memory)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version,name,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
- docker run --gpus all -it --rm --shm-size=1g --ulimit memlock=-1:262144 my-image:latest bash
- python -u -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available()); a=torch.randn(1024,1024,device='cuda'); print(a.device)"
- LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:/opt/nvidia/lib python train.py

Errors / snippets captured:
- RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 8.00 GiB total capacity; 6.10 GiB already allocated)
  - happened despite small batch sizes; memory reported 'already allocated' indicates possible leaking allocator or KV cache not being freed.

- CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED when calling cuBLASCreate_v2
  - often synonymous with OOM at startup / fragmentation.

- CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
  - observed when image has toolkit 12.x but host driver 510.x.

- dmesg: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31, pid=12345, name=python
  NVRM: Xid 31 is generic hang; often kernel/driver mismatch or device reset.

- ImportError: libcuda.so.1: version `NVIDIA-ABI-NONSTD-5' not found 
  - indicates ABI mismatch between packaged libcuda and installed driver.

Hypotheses:
1) Mismatched CUDA toolkit vs driver on host <-> container leading to subtle failures (libcuda mismatch).
2) Torch wheel linked to a different cuBLAS/cuDNN set than system driver supports — at runtime large pinned allocations fail.
3) Memory fragmentation / leaking allocator in our inference runtime: we saw "already allocated" balloon over repeated requests.
4) Kernel-level GPU reset (Xid 31) triggered by bad driver + high mem use during JIT/compilation.

What I tried (and results):
- Rebuilt container with pytorch wheel for target CUDA (11.8) and tested with host driver 525.85 -> passes short smoke tests.
- Reproduced failure on older driver 510.x paired with same image -> got "driver version is insufficient" error.
- Switched to nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime base image -> reduces ABI errors but still saw OOM after long loop.
- Inserted torch.cuda.empty_cache() and del(local_vars) at end of batch loop -> delayed OOM but did not prevent it entirely.
- Ran with TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1 (debug sparse allocator) -> not available on wheel, no effect.

Kernel / system traces I captured:
- sudo journalctl -k | grep NVRM -n
  [output snippet] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31, pid=2468, name=python
- dmesg | tail -n 60 -> shows GPU reset and device lost messages right before container crash.

Bisect plan (practical):
- Step A: Confirm reproducibility on host (non-container): run small script that loops allocations and frees and logs torch.cuda.memory_allocated() each iter.
  - If fails on host -> likely driver/systems issue.
  - If only fails in container -> container runtime mismatch.
- Step B: matrix test across driver versions (510, 515, 525, 535) + CUDA runtimes (11.8, 12.0, 12.1) using a small k8s job in CI; pivot on first combination that fails reproducing the OOM.
- Step C: use NVTX ranges + torch.cuda.memory_summary() to find hotspots and possible leak points.
- Step D: run strace on Python process to see if there are frequent mmap calls that grow resident set size and could indicate a host-side allocation issue.

Useful commands / snippets to run again: 
- python -c "import torch, gc; print(torch.cuda.memory_summary());
  for i in range(200):
    x = torch.randn(1024,1024, device='cuda')
    if i % 20 == 0: print(i, torch.cuda.memory_allocated())
    del x; gc.collect(); torch.cuda.empty_cache()"

- docker run --gpus all --shm-size=4g -e NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all --rm my-image bash -c "python reproduce.py 2>&1 | tee /tmp/repro.log"

- cat /var/log/nvidia-installer.log
- rpm -qa | grep nvidia (for RHEL systems)
- apt list --installed | grep nvidia (for Debian)

Notes / small findings:
- On my laptop the problem correlated with a specific third-party plugin that called cuInit twice from different languages (node addon + python extension) — caused weird state. Removing plugin eliminated Xid 31.
- In CI we use an older host driver pinned to 510 for compatibility with older machines; that environment is more brittle.
- Increasing --shm-size in docker helped one flaky job that failed with OOM on shared tensors (IPC).

Immediate TODOs / handoff checklist:
- Re-run matrix in a disposable k8s namespace and collect nvidia-smi logs every 30s. Upload to: https://s3.redwood.ai/debug/gpu-bisect/<date>
- If Xid 31 occurs, capture full dmesg and coredump (if configured). File an INC with kernel logs attached.
- Try rebuild of minimal wheel using the same CUDA ABI as the host driver and run again.

Notes for SRE handoff:
- Machine: dev-laptop-01 (PCI:0000:01:00) + ci-node-07 (k8s, GPU pool)
- Approx steps to reproduce: 'docker run ... reproduce.py --iters 400 --batch 2'
- Logs: /tmp/repro.log, /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, dmesg output.

Random ideas (future):
- Add a small watchdog to the runtime that dumps torch.cuda.memory_summary() and NVTX markers when resident memory increases > 10% inside 30s window.
- Try running with NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=none and using cpu-only run to validate no host memory pressure correlation.

If I come back to this later, next checkpoint: finish driver vs toolkit matrix (Step B) and collect NVTX traces for one failing and one passing run to diff.

-- end of scratchpad --
